piezas.titulo: How Wikipedia’s Editors Keep the Online Encyclopedia Human-Written
piezas.resumenOriginal: Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup , a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove AI-generated material from Wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia. When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material? Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage.” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this. Ellia Lebleu Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph.D. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes , part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology. How do editors spot AI-generated writing today? Lebleu: By 2025, the signs of AI writing were becoming subtler and more structural. For example, AI loves the “rule of three,” negative parallelisms, and other structures of speech that aren’t conclusive by themselves but become meaningful as they accumulate. We also look beyond the article. If someone writes five articles of thousands of words each in 5 minutes, there is reason to suspect AI. Does the AI problem just appear in the main text, or also in citations? Lebleu: Fake or misleading citations have become a major worry. Sometimes an AI hallucinates a citation entirely, although that’s much rarer today because of retrieval-augmented generation that allows the AI to find sources. More often, it finds a real source but gets its content completely wrong. AI citations that don’t actually support what is being written are extremely commonplace. English Wikipedia recently prohibited editors from using LLMs to generate articles. How much AI-generated content is still getting through? Lebleu: I’ve been working with [AI-detection company] Pangram to estimate the proportion of AI-generated content. I tested it on Wikipedia content from before ChatGPT and found no false positives, so its results provide a very conservative lower bound. In late 2025, it flagged perhaps 20 percent of new articles and drafts as AI-generated. In early 2026, that went down to 15 or 16 percent. But we don’t yet know whether that’s because our recent policies have had an effect or because models are getting more powerful and Pangram hasn’t had time to adapt. Is Wikipedia using AI to combat AI? Lebleu: Another Wikipedia editor has made an AI source verifier, which goes through the sources on a page and checks whether they match the claims. Since it is itself an AI model, there is no guarantee that it will be correct every time. But if you want something that works at scale and filters out obvious cases, it’s a good first step. The Wikimedia Foundation is also working on a tool called Paste Check , which can flag text pasted directly from some AI chatbots. And we’ve seen Claude sometimes say, “I can’t write a Wikipedia article; it would go against Wikipedia’s policies.” If all major AI companies implemented that kind of prompt refusal, it wouldn’t solve the problem entirely, because there are still open-weight models that can be tweaked to avoid restrictions. But it would help with people who use commercial models and aren’t especially familiar with the technology. Can you tell if the rule prohibiting AI writing is working? Lebleu: It’s still a little early to tell. We see possible effects, such as prompt refusal and the apparent slight drop in AI-generated content. But again, we don’t yet know if that is because models are getting better or because beginners are learning the rules. The vast majority of AI-generated content is submitted by beginner editors, so we’ve made many efforts to make the rule very visible in welcome messages, editing help, and advice. What if AI becomes capable of writing truly reliable Wikipedia articles? Lebleu: That’s one of the big questions we’re facing. When the guideline was passed, it was for very practical reasons: We were flooded with AI content, we didn’t have good tools, and we needed to put a stop to it. But since then, it has taken on a more philosophical dimension. Many people have called Wikipedia “the last good place on the internet.” Being a place that was, in theory, free from AI slop has become part of Wikipedia’s identity. A lot of Wikipedia’s communication is now centered on the idea that we’re a human-written encyclopedia. Even AI companies find that interesting. It can be valuable to have a purely human-written corpus on which to [train] AI systems. The fact that Wikipedia is still that, and will remain that for at least the near future, makes it a precious resource that isn’t replicated anywhere else. But will the people who read and contribute to Wikipedia want it to become partially AI-generated if that makes it more comprehensive? We could preserve Wikipedia’s identity as a human-written corpus while also offering an AI-assisted option. Has Wikipedia reckoned with the idea of “Google Zero”—a possible future in which websites no longer get traffic from Google search? Lebleu: If everything goes through AI search and websites plummet to zero visibility, how do we expose Wikipedia and show that it can be edited and that people can still contribute? Wikipedia is frequently cited in [Google’s] AI Overviews, but users may only see an AI answer citing Wikipedia. They may not realize that Wikipedia is a living project they can edit and contribute to. The Wikimedia Foundation is working on an attribution framework that could give AI users more information about the article [being cited]: when it was last edited, how comprehensive it is, whether editors have flagged problems, and perhaps even a call to action. In the future, readers might even contribute through AI models: “The AI cited Wikipedia, but there seems to be an error. Can I make an edit request and add this other source I found?” I can see a very strong symbiotic relationship between Wikipedia and AI models in the future. I don’t see Wikipedia disappearing, but I can see it taking a very different shape. Yesterday, AI was something to clean up. Today, it’s a tool to help us with the cleanup. Tomorrow, it will be the air we breathe. A condensed version of this article appears in the November 2026 print issue as “Ellia Lebleu.”

piezas.titulo: Functional and Structural Brain Age Gaps as Complementary Predictive Markers for Cognitive Performance
piezas.resumenOriginal: Cognitive decline is characterized by substantial inter-individual variability across the lifespan, even among clinically healthy adults. However, it is unclear how structural and functional brain organization jointly relate to differences in cognitive performance within the typical populations. We considered a multimodal brain age framework by predicting for each subject its age from either structural MRI or resting-state functional MRI, after training on the 1000BRAINS cohort (901 participants, 18-85 years). Following, a structural and a functional brain age gap markers were defined as the deviations with respect to the real chronological age. We then used the markers to characterize the interplay between structure and function in shaping cognitive performances. Our findings reveal that the functional marker is as important to predict global cognitive performance as the structural marker. The most accurate prediction was found for global cognition, executive functions and episodic memory, followed by working memory, attention and language. In particular, the structural marker was contributing to all domains, except for working memory, whereas the functional marker had the highest contribution. Overall, structural and functional brain age models together provide a meaningful subject-level summary of brain information for predicting cognition, supporting a multidimensional view of typical aging.

piezas.titulo: An exploratory study of relationships between the executive functions and spatiotemporal control in a complex motor task: the spatial tapping task
piezas.resumenOriginal: Executive functions (EFs) are cognitive processes enabling planning, control, and regulation of behavior. A variety of tasks have been developed to evaluate EFs, from complex reasoning to simpler inhibition tasks, reflecting the diversity of symptoms observed in patients with executive deficits. Recent research has emphasized their unity, proposing three core functions, working memory, inhibition, and switching, that share resources and combine to enable complex tasks. Yet, no single task captures both the unity and diversity of EFs, limiting the development of a unified framework and a balanced assessment. To address this gap, we designed the spatial tapping task, a timing paradigm combining finger tapping and circle drawing. Finger tapping requires working memory for explicit timing control, whereas circle drawing requires anticipatory control akin to switching to control movement trajectory, enabling implicit timing control. Participants produce taps along a circular trajectory with the tempo increasing progressively. A slow tempo favors discrete movements with long pauses between taps, whereas a fast tempo promotes continuous motion. Previous analyses supported a change in timing control mode with increasing tempo. Here, we explored the hypothesis that EFs are engaged accordingly: working memory in the slow/discrete phase, switching in the fast/continuous phase, and inhibition in the intermediate phase, where demands for continuous motion increase. In two studies combined into a single dataset, we compared scores with those from neuropsychological tests using correlations. We found that timing accuracy in the slow/discrete phase was associated with working memory, spatial accuracy in the fast/continuous phase with switching, and longer contact time in the intermediate phase with inhibition. We also explored whether performance was consistent with the EF deficits described in the literature, and the potential contribution of motor output, reporting scores obtained across populations with executive deficits (aging and dementia), combined executive and motor impairments (schizophrenia), and motor expertise (biscriptual writers), along with matched controls. Findings were consistent, although often more specific, and highlighted an important contribution of motor output. Altogether, our results provide initial evidence that the task can be used to investigate EFs, although cognitive, motor, and sensory contributions need to be disentangled to improve its specificity.

piezas.titulo: High-dimensional hippocampus representation facilitates learning of low-dimensional abstract representation and supports generalization
piezas.resumenOriginal: Semantic knowledge encompasses facts, concepts, and their relationships. Recent work has proposed that some forms of semantic knowledge could be encoded in low-dimensional neural representations, such as the abstract, disentangled representational geometries observed in many cognitive brain areas. Experimental work has shown that hippocampal (HPC) lesions impair the formation of flexible and generalizable semantic knowledge. However, HPC representations are often high-dimensional and sparse. How can these representations contribute to the formation of low-dimensional abstract representation across these cognitive cortical areas? Here, we reconcile these observations using multiregional neural network models. Modeling HPC as a sparse, decorrelating autoencoder, we show that its high-dimensional representations promote the robust and efficient formation of low-dimensional abstract representations in downstream regions such as prefrontal cortex. This effect is most pronounced when the geometry of sensory inputs is misaligned with the geometry of desired outputs, requiring a more complex input-output transformation. Mathematical analysis shows that hippocampal expansion recoding suppresses misleading low-dimensional input structure and reshapes the loss landscape of downstream networks, allowing abstract semantic geometry to emerge reliably. The resulting abstract representations provide an inductive bias for sample-efficient learning of novel semantic-to-action mappings. Finally, we show that consolidating hippocampus-dependent representations into a hippocampus-independent pathway improves out-of-distribution generalization based on input structure. Together, these results suggest a circuit mechanism by which high-dimensional hippocampal representations can support, rather than oppose, the emergence of low-dimensional abstract representations.

piezas.titulo: A non-randomized trial of the effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on cognitive performance and resting state connectivity
piezas.resumenOriginal: BackgroundTranscutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has shown promise for enhancing cognition and emotion regulation. To date, most human studies have focused on narrow learning paradigms that limit our understanding of how taVNS influences complex, integrative cognitive operations. Moreover, the underlying mechanisms of taVNS are still not well understood.ObjectiveBuilding on preclinical findings that vagus nerve stimulation enhances cognitive flexibility and memory in animal models, this study investigated whether acute taVNS can modulate executive function and neural connectivity in healthy adults.MethodsUsing a quasi-experimental design, forty healthy participants received either active or sham taVNS while completing executive function tasks and adaptive cognitive training (BrainHQ). High-density electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded during stimulation to assess cortical activity and functional connectivity across frequency bands.ResultsMultivariate analyses demonstrated significant effects of taVNS on cognitive function and EEG. Post-hoc group comparisons showed that compared to sham stimulation, active taVNS was associated with improved BrainHQ performance and decreased delta-band connectivity in left frontal, central, and parietal regions. Delta-band connectivity during active taVNS was positively associated with pre-to-post improvements in mood. No difference in executive function tasks was found between active and sham taVNS. Sensitivity analyses using adjusted models showed that these effects were sensitive to age, sex, and education.ConclusionBy evaluating multiple dimensions of executive function, these exploratory findings suggest that active taVNS may influence selected aspects of executive performance and frontal–parietal delta connectivity, potentially reflecting enhanced neural efficiency arising from the interaction between vagally mediated neuromodulation and continuously adaptive cognitive demands. However, these effects did not survive multiple-comparison correction and should therefore be interpreted cautiously and replicated in larger, prospectively powered studies.

Esta reducción podría indicar una mayor eficiencia neural durante tareas adaptativas, aunque no alteró los resultados de pruebas ejecutivas tradicionales.
